title: US senator proposes AI crisis hotline with China
key_facts: Sen. Maria Cantwell, ranking Democrat on the Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee, proposed a US-China emergency channel for AI incidents.
Modelled on the Cold War Washington-Moscow hotline; for a major AI malfunction or loss of control over an autonomous system.

Part of a six-point framework released Wednesday 7 Oct 2026: NIST safety standards, independent audits before release, continuous testing, legal accountability, international cooperation, export-control coordination.
Also covers worker protections, children's safety and human review of consequential AI decisions.
The framework is a policy proposal, not enacted legislation.
Roll Call: it contrasts with the White House focus on voluntary standards; Cruz chairs the committee.
quote_evidence: The proposed mechanism would allow the two countries to communicate rapidly if a major AI malfunction, loss of control over an autonomous system or other serious incident threatened either country’s security.
The framework is a policy proposal, not enacted legislation.
why_it_matters_hint: A proposal for a US-China emergency line for AI accidents.
notes: Read at IANS (own wire text). The Hans India carries the same copy. Roll Call and PYMNTS confirm the framework and that it has no legislative text.
